QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_5

question.text: For a trading member in cash-settled IRD on G-Sec (8-11 year bucket), the open interest is INR 10,000 crore. What is the trading-member position limit?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, the TM limit for cash-settled G-Sec IRD in the 8-11 year bucket is 10% of open interest or INR 1,200 crore (equivalent to 60,000 lots), whichever is higher. 10% of INR 10,000 crore = INR 1,000 crore. Higher of INR 1,000 crore and INR 1,200 crore = INR 1,200 crore. The Trap: INR 1,000 crore applies only the percentage and ignores the absolute floor. INR 600 crore is the absolute floor for the 4-8 / 11-15 year buckets, not 8-11 year. INR 1,500 crore is not a source-backed figure and the "lower of 15% market-wide / Rs. 1,000 crore" formula is not in the workbook for G-Sec futures. Note: Pages 234-237 set out higher-of category limits keyed off open interest. For 91-day T-Bill / Overnight MIBOR, the workbook prescribes a different rule (15% of total open interest or Rs. 1,000 crore, higher of).
